title: A strided dot product
hints: A stride is just how far apart consecutive elements sit in memory.
Loop `i` from 0 to `n - 1` and multiply `a[i*sa]` by `b[i*sb]`, adding into a running sum.
Start the sum at 0 so `n = 0` returns 0, and use the strides on both arrays: a column of a row-major matrix has stride equal to its row length.

answer.explain: The reference accumulates `a[i*sa] * b[i*sb]` for `i` in `0 .. n-1`. Scaling each index by its own stride lets the same function dot a row (stride 1) with a column (stride N).
